newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move mirroring the Victorian Government's successful sale of TABCorp Holdings Ltd, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr announced yesterday his Government would publicly float its Totalisator Agency Board (TAB), but will exclude gaming companies from buying any shares in the company. Page 1.

Former Coles Myer finance director John Barner, who already has two actions pending against Coles, has along with his company Spring Street Management Services, which held Coles Myer options, lodged a Supreme Court writ alleging unconscionable conduct aganst the retail giant and is seeking to restore entitlements to share options and superannuation revoked when he resigned in April 1995. Page 3.

Australians will soon get their first chance to invest directly in a major electricity generator, after the Victorian Government confirmed yesterday the Horizon Energy consortium - led by US utilities CMS Generation and NRG Energy Inc - had won a three-way battle to acquire the State's Loy Yang A power station. Page 21.

Under a deal that will form a company ranked among the top four Australian wine producers, contract wine processor Simeon Wines Ltd has secured a friendly takeover of Australian Vintage Ltd. The A$111 million scrip and cash offer comprised of four Simeon shares and A$3.60 cash for every five AustVin shares. Page 21.

Country Road's Japanese partner, Itochu, the Wooltru group in South Africa, and the United States-based retail group The Gap are among the companies rumoured to have paid about A$15 million for a 15 per cent stake in Country Road. The mystery investor is believed to have been analysing such an investment for some months. Page 21.

Simsmetal Ltd shares rose 27 cents yesterday to A$8.22 as investors responded positively to a A$22.1 million net profit for the nine months to March 31, with earnings in the third quarter rising a solid 38 per cent to A$8 million after tax. The positive response came despite the fact that the metal recycling company was still 35 per cent below the previous nine month result. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a surprisingly hardline stance against the outcome of the living wage claim, the Business Council of Australia claimed yesterday the decision introduced a systematic fault into the wages system, with president Stan Wallis saying equity considerations sould not be addressed in the wages system. The Australian Chamber of Commerce also criticised the move, saying it could inhibit this year's expected manufacturing recovery. Page 21.

A meeting of trustees from the New South Wales Government-owned funds management business Axiom on Monday is believed to have approved German finance house Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and the National Australia Bank as potential bidders, rating them well clear of other bidders in the A$200 million war for Axiom. Page 21.

A total of 7.6 million of troubled upmarket clothing retailer Country Road's 52 million shares were specialled by broker JB Were yesterday, in what could be a takeover bid from a foreign company. The mystery buyer or buyers, who bought the stake at A$2-a-hare, 30 cents above the prevailing market price, was unknown yesterday. Page 21.

Optus finance director Michael Stefanovski is to temporarily fill the position of chief financial officer following the shock resignation of David Amer, who was one of two executive officers on the Optus board, along with chief executive Ziggy Switkowski. The move is a hurdle to the A$4 billion float of Optus Communications and a replacement is being urgently sought. Page 23.

New Grains Council president Brendan Stewart is meeting with Federal Primary Industries Minister John Anderson today to lobby the Federal Government to clarify key aspects of its plan to restructure the Australian Wheat Board. The Coalition's plan would se a commercial board operating two subsidiaries through a holding company after July 1999. Page 23.

Three St Barbara Mines Ltd directors - Peter Jones, Norman Bevan and Leslie Nixon - reacted angrily yesterday to recently appointed director Ross Atkins' claims to the Australian Stock Exchange that two senior company executives who resigned were impropery reinstated. The directors said Atkins' claim was materially wrong and constituted an unauthorised release. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The New South Wales Government announced yesterday that four companies that were keen to buy NSW TAB - Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd, AWA AWA AX, TABCorp TAH.AX and Tattersalls - have been prevented from participating in the estimated A$1 billion float of the gaming buiness. In addition, no shareholder will be able to own more than five per cent of TAB. Page 29.

The new owner of a 50 per cent stake in Victoria's Loy Yang A power station, United States-based CMS Energy, has justified the record A$4.855 billion price tag for the station by saying New South Wales electricity prices would have to increase soon - a comment increasing pressure on the current structure of the State's electricity industry. Page 29.

Economists have reacted positively to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission's awarding of a A$10-a-week wage increase to thousands of Australian workers, saying it was a prudent move which would see business and consumers enjoying lower inflation down the track and that it showed inflation was dead - at least for the rest of 1997. Page 29.

Speaking at a three-and-a-half hour general meeting yesterday, Australian Provincial Newspapers Holdings APN.AX chief executive Cameron O'Reilly reassured shareholders that the group was on the road to recovery from a flat 1996 result, revealing its regional newpaper division made a reasonable start to 1997 and predicting an improvement in this year's earnings. Page 31.

As the Federal Government considers easing cross-media ownership rules as a means of adding to the diversity of ownership in the national newspaper market, several Australian groups have approached British-based Pearson Plc PSON.L suggesting a partnership to bid for The Australian Financial Review. Page 31.

According to a survey of 5,000 businesses by Monash University, funded by National Mutual, about 80 per cent of family businesses do not have any plans for succession, with first-generation firms less likely to become multiple-generation businesses becaus their original intention was to exit the market. Page 31.
THE AGE

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett said yesterday's sale of the State's Loy Yang A power station to US -based Horizon Energy for A$4885 million puts pressure on the New South Wales Government to follow his lead and privatise its own electricity industry. Kenett praised the deal, calling it the largest of its kind ever witnessed in Australia, and said it cements Victoria as the leader of the country's power industries. Page B1.

The sharemarket reacted positively to yesterday's news the ACTU's A$20-a-week living wage claim was rejected by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission, replaced by a A$10-a-week rise. The Australian dollar closed at 77.57 cents, and the bond markt traded firmly amid hopes of a interest rate cut. Page B1.

Country Road has denied knowledge of the mystery buyer of almost 15 per cent of the fashion group's issued capital yesterday, estimated at around A$15 million. Whilst it is not believed the Lew family was involved in yesterday's trading, speculators belive the flurry of buying could have come from Country Road's 25 per cent partner in Japan, Itouchu, or South Africa's Select group which controls the Sportsgirl fashion chain. Page B3.

New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has closed the door on any major players in the gaming industry from owning a piece of the soon to be privatised NSW TAB. Carr's announcement that no single company will be able to own more that five per cent of the bettig company will restrict the four large companies interested in the privatisation - PBL, AWA, Tabcorp and Tattersalls - from investing in TAB shares. Page B3.

Resolute RSG.AX yesterday gained the backing of Citibank for its race to become Western Australia's next nickel producer, putting it at the head of the five other mining companies all trying to secure market share before mining giant Inco N.TO starts developing the Voisey Bay discovery in north-east Canada. Page B3.

WMC WMC.AX has failed to provide details of its mining operations in the Philippines in its latest quarterly report, despite market concerns. WMC's new Tampakan copper project, which could become one of the world's largest copper projects, has the potential of boosting the company's copper productions to a point where it would rival the world's major producers of the metal. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
